title: Orchid Therapeutics: Privacy Assertions & Archive Policy Review
summary: Orchid requested confirmation on data handling guarantees: no customer data used for model training, configurable prompt retention/archival policies, KMS-backed encryption with HSM support, RBAC/SSO integration details, and audit log exports. Redwood AE/SE walked through controls, provided clarifying details on ephemeral prompt handling, dual-key KMS offering for Private deployments, and proposed an audit trail export for compliance. Agreed next steps: share SOC 2/ISO artifacts, draft archival policy options, schedule a short pilot to validate audit log format.
topics: Prompt + content retention vs archival policies
Encryption architecture: KMS, HSM, dual-key options
Audit logs, export formats, and retention windows
Data residency and Private deployment considerations
transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Dr. Priya Rao (Orchid): Priya here. Hey Lena, Tom and Maya on our side.
[00:10] Tom Alvarez (Orchid): Hi, yes.
[00:12] Maya Venkat (Orchid): Hello.
[00:15] Marcus (Redwood SE): Marcus joining. We'll dive into the controls and technical bits.
[00:22] Lena: Agenda — SOC 2/ISO evidence, prompt retention, encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and then open Qs and next steps. Does that cover it for you Priya?
[00:32] Dr. Priya: Yep, that's perfect. Main ask up front: we need an explicit statement that customer prompts and content are not used to train Redwood models, and we need detail on how long prompts are kept, where they're stored, and ability to archive or delete.
[00:46] Lena: Absolutely. High level: hosted API by default retains prompts for 30 days for safety and abuse detection unless you opt-in to longer retention; we offer an enterprise setting for no retention for customer accounts, and Private deployments keep all control with you. But Marcus will go deeper on the technical enforcement.
[01:02] Marcus: Right. For hosted customers who select the "no retention" flag, we implement a disk-level ephemeral path and do not persist user prompts beyond transient caching used for streaming; logs are truncated and scrubbed. For Dedicated/Private, you control the storage lifecycle — you can set retention=0 and we don't ship any data back to central models.
[01:18] Tom: When you say "don't ship back to central models", does that mean absolutely no training pipeline sees our data? Are there any aggregated telemetry feeds used to improve models?
[01:29] Marcus: Good question. For accounts with the no-retention configuration and enterprise contract, we don't send those prompts into any model fine-tuning or training queues. We do collect anonymized service metrics (e.g., latency percentiles, request sizes) for operational purposes but they are not tied back to prompt text.
[01:44] Dr. Priya: How do you technically enforce that? Is it a configuration flag, or separate logical tenancy? We need an auditable control.
[01:52] Marcus: It's two-fold: tenancy-level policy + pipeline guards. The request router attaches an account tag; downstream ingestion services have an allowlist/denylist check. If retention=0, the pipeline drops payloads at the first persistence point. We also have automated integration tests that run in CI to validate the deny path. We can provide logs from those tests.
[02:12] Maya: We'd want cryptographic proof or at least signed attestations. SOC 2 cover some of this but we also require regular attestations.
[02:21] Lena: We can share SOC 2 type II report and ISO 27001 certificate. For customer-specific attestations we can provide a short letter confirming contractual constraints, and for Private deployments you can run your own audits.
[02:34] Tom: Speaking of encryption, what's the KMS story? Can we bring our own key?
[02:39] Marcus: Yes. Hosted supports BYOK via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault). We have an optional double-encryption mode where the customer key wraps a data key and Redwood also has a service key — DOUBLE key separation — or for Private installs you can use a local HSM and we never see your keys.
[02:55] Dr. Priya: Double-key sounds interesting. For compliance we might prefer we hold the master key. Does that break functionality like auto-scaling?
[03:04] Marcus: It introduces a small latency (few tens of milliseconds per key unwrap) but auto-scaling remains functional. We cache unwrapped data keys in a secure enclave for a configurable short window to avoid repeated unwraps under heavy traffic.
[03:18] Lena: On RBAC and SSO, we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning for user sync, and role-based policies (admin, auditor, developer, read-only). We also expose token-level scopes for API keys so you can limit actions programmatically.
[03:33] Maya: Can we restrict access so only specific roles can see prompt text in audit logs?
[03:38] Marcus: Yes. Audit logs are split: metadata logs (request id, timestamp, model, latency) are default, full-text logs are gated and require a role 'prompt_reader' and are encrypted with a customer-specific key if requested.
[03:52] Tom: Format of audit exports? We need to ingest them into our SIEM.
[03:56] Marcus: We can ship logs in JSON Lines, with gzip optional, and S3-compatible endpoints for delivery. For Private deployments logs can be written directly to your object store. We also support syslog streaming.
[04:10] Dr. Priya: Retention policy options — you mentioned 30 days default. Can you give the full range?
[04:16] Lena: Defaults: 30 days for hosted standard. Enterprise: configurable 0–730 days. For Dedicated you can request custom retention and for Private it's whatever you configure. We can also support an archival tier where logs older than X days get moved to cold storage and encrypted with a different key.
[04:33] Maya: If we set 0 retention, are there any ephemeral copies left in caches or backups?
[04:38] Marcus: No persistent backups of prompt text are taken when retention=0. We do use short-lived caches for streaming and KV cache entries may exist transiently in memory or NVMe cache; those caches are scrubbed on eviction and are not part of backups. We can provide cache eviction timing details for your auditors.
[04:56] Tom: About data residency — our data cannot leave EU. Does Redwood have options to pin to a region?
[05:02] Lena: Yes, we have region pinning for hosted — EU-only tenancy that keeps compute and storage in EU regions. For stricter controls we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.
[05:12] Dr. Priya: Any customers using Private inside our cloud?
[05:15] Marcus: We've done Private installs in customer VPCs for several regulated pharma customers; we can share redacted architecture diagrams.
[05:23] Maya: Audit trail integrity — do you support immutable append-only logs?
[05:28] Marcus: We expose write-once append stores (WORM) as an option, or we can configure S3 Object Lock for a retention period. Logs are shipped with SHA256 digests and you can verify integrity client-side.
[05:40] Dr. Priya: For the "no-train" clause: do you allow sub-processors or partners that might use aggregate data?
[05:47] Lena: Sub-processors used for infra (cloud providers) only receive encrypted blobs; we do not hand off plaintext prompts. Any analytic partners would only see aggregated telemetry not raw prompts — and those partners are in our sub-processor list. We can provide a current sub-processor list and contractual controls (DPA).
[06:05] Tom: Legal will want contractual language that prohibits training on our data. Can Redwood commit to contractual no-training language?
[06:12] Lena: Yes, we have contract language we use for enterprise customers that explicitly prohibits model training on customer-provided content and mandates data handling controls. We'll share a sample addendum.
[06:22] Maya: We also want to confirm deletion procedures if a user requests deletion — how do you handle in-flight requests and delete-at-rest?
[06:29] Marcus: Delete requests trigger a tombstone and an asynchronous purge job that walks object stores and KV caches; for hosted, purge latency is typically under 24 hours but we can negotiate faster SLA in enterprise contracts. For real-time expunge we can also provide a retention=0 real-time path.
[06:48] Dr. Priya: Can you produce proof-of-deletion for an individual prompt?
[06:53] Marcus: We can provide deletion logs showing request id, timestamp, and the storage keys that were removed. For cryptographic proof, we can provide signed deletion attestations that reference the sha256 of the object that was removed.
[07:06] Tom: On SOC 2 / ISO artifacts — what can you share now and what requires an NDA or customer status?
[07:13] Lena: SOC 2 type II summary and ISO certificate we can share after an NDA. Full SOC 2 report is available under an NDA and usually requires a channel partner NDA. We can initiate that today.
[07:25] Maya: Will you also share penetration test results or at least a redacted executive summary?
[07:30] Marcus: We can provide executive summaries of pen tests and vulnerability management metrics, redacted to remove PoC detail.
[07:36] Dr. Priya: For the pilot we want to run a short smoke test to validate the audit logs and deletion flows. How long would that take?
[07:43] Lena: We can stand up a short pilot in 2–3 weeks for hosted enterprise with no-retention settings and a log export endpoint. Dedicated/Private takes longer.
[07:53] Tom: Are there additional charges for BYOK or double-key mode?
[07:57] Marcus: BYOK itself isn't an extra charge but double-key and HSM-backed private key management options incur a configuration fee and slight monthly premium to cover HSM costs and operational support. We'll include estimates in the follow-up.
[08:10] Maya: Can you confirm the audit log schema — field names, sample payload? We need to map it to our SIEM fields.
[08:16] Marcus: Yes we'll share a sample JSON Lines schema. Fields: request_id, account_id, timestamp, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, user_id (if propagated), prompt_hash (sha256), prompt_text (optional/gated), response_hash, response_text (optional/gated), retention_flag. We'll also provide example files.
[08:36] Dr. Priya: What about PII/PHI handling — if a prompt contains PHI, do you do any automated scrubbing?
[08:42] Marcus: We provide optional PII redaction features — regex/NER-based scrubbers that can run in the request path or as a post-processing job. We also support customer-provided scrubber modules for Private deployments. These are configurable per-route.
[08:58] Tom: If we use scrubbers, are the originals retained anywhere?
[09:02] Marcus: Originals are only retained if retention policy permits. If you have retention=0 and scrubbers are configured to operate inline, originals are never persisted. If you need full archival of originals for clinical audit, we support that as a separate encrypted archive with different key management.
[09:18] Lena: Quick pause — any other blockers we should be aware of?
[09:22] Maya: For legal the big things: contractual no-training clause, proof-of-deletion artifacts, and SOC2/ISO artifacts and sub-processor list.
[09:30] Dr. Priya: InfoSec wants to validate the double-key flow and see latency impact and key lifecycle docs.
[09:36] Lena: We'll produce an action pack.
[09:39] Marcus: A couple of technical notes: streaming responses may buffer small chunks server-side for efficient decode; those buffers are ephemeral and covered by retention policies. Also, KV cache entries for long-running conversations are only kept to speed up inference and are purged per retention policy.
[09:58] Tom: For our auditors, can you provide a mapping of your controls to common frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO controls)?
[10:04] Lena: Yes, we have a controls mapping doc. We'll attach it.
[10:08] Maya: One more: can you restrict debug dumps so they exclude prompt text unless explicitly authorized?
[10:13] Marcus: Debug dumps are redacted by default; full dumps require an elevated role and are audited.
[10:19] Dr. Priya: Great. Let's talk timeline: you'll share artifacts, we review, then pilot.
[10:25] Lena: Correct. We'll send SOC2/ISO under NDA, sample audit logs, sample deletion attestation, contract addendum language, and an estimate for double-key/HSM. Aim to have the pilot kickoff in ~3 weeks.
[10:38] Maya: Sounds good.
[10:40] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[10:44] Lena: Thanks — we'll recap actions.
[10:46] [Meeting ends]

Share sample audit-log JSON Lines schema and example files
Provide sample contractual addendum with explicit no-training language
